guide.title: Who decides whether a message is marketing
guide.subtitle: The message type is a declaration, not a guess
guide.excerpt: The platform asks you to declare what kind of message you are sending instead of inferring it from the text. That one field decides whether the opt-out gate applies — and the honesty of the declaration is yours.

p: A send request carries a message type: MARKETING, INFORMATIONAL or TRANSACTIONAL. Exactly one of those three passes through the opt-out gate, and it is MARKETING. Order confirmations, one-time codes and password resets are not blocked by a recipient’s earlier STOP, because a person who opted out of promotions still needs their login to work.
The gate is deliberately narrow. It blocks a single category, and it blocks it before the provider is ever called — so a suppressed message never reaches the carrier and is not billed.

sections.h: Why the platform does not read your message
p: The platform does not analyze message bodies. It cannot: bodies are not stored, and the gate runs before anything is handed to a provider. That means the declaration is the only input, and a promotional message declared as TRANSACTIONAL will pass.

Passing is not the same as being permitted. In jurisdictions such as the US under the TCPA, a reminder that carries promotional content is still marketing in law, and sending it to someone who opted out is a violation — regardless of the type you declared.

sections.h: Why the default is the strict one
list: Omitting the field means MARKETING, the most restrictive value. If you forget it, you over-block; you never under-block.
An unrecognised value is rejected with an error rather than silently downgraded. A typo should surface as a broken integration, not as verification codes that quietly stop arriving.
Marketing and transactional traffic should be split on your side, not merged and re-labeled per send.
sections.scope: The opt-out gate is implemented for the SMS channel. Email and WhatsApp connect on the same model but do not carry this gate today.
